papers.title_in_file: QuMoS: A Framework for Preserving Security of Quantum Machine Learning Model
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, II Threat Model, III Design, V Evaluation (setup and main results), VII Conclusion; Section IV (RL engine details) and VI (related work) skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A framework that splits a quantum machine learning model across several quantum cloud providers, with a reinforcement learning search, to resist model stealing.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on four datasets, the QuMoS model design reaches accuracy close to a model found by neural architecture search under centralized settings, while giving the highest security among the baselines they compare.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p1; Section V results, Table I
quotes: Experimental results on four datasets show that the model design proposed by QuMoS can achieve a close accuracy to the model designed with neural architecture search under centralized settings while providing the highest security than the baselines.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small downsampled image tasks.
assertions.reader_inference: Security here is the paper's own heuristic metric, not a formal guarantee.

assertions.value: The authors state that an untrustworthy quantum cloud provider could query the QML service with its own data and, because quantum circuits are reversible, build a reverse circuit to recover the model.
quotes: Assume that the quantum cloud provider is untrustworthy, then it could send arbitrary data D(Z) to query the QML service, pretending as an ordinary user.
Since the quantum circuit is reversible, the attacker could build the reverse quantum circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: The attack is argued in text; the paper does not run it.

assertions.value: The authors state that accuracy was evaluated on the first 300 test images because of limited quantum computing resources.
quotes: And we used the first 300 images in the test set to evaluate the accuracy of the QML models due to the limited quantum computing resources.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation scope, Section V-A.
assertions.reader_inference: Accuracy differences of under one percent are within sampling noise for 300 images.

papers.title_in_file: Several fitness functions and entanglement gates in quantum kernel generation
papers.version_note: File title differs from the filename (filename says 'Generating quantum feature maps using multi-objective genetic'); same arXiv id 2309.03307, v3. Treated as the same paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 5 experiment setup, 6 Conclusion and Discussion; sections 2 to 4 and the result figures skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A multi-objective genetic algorithm study of how many entanglement (CNOT) gates a quantum-kernel feature map needs, on two small classical datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the optimal quantum-kernel circuit configuration found by their genetic algorithm contains a proportional number of non-local entanglement gates, in contrast to prior work in which such gates were largely suppressed.
quotes: Our experiments reveal that the optimal configuration of quantum circuits for the quantum kernel method incorporates a proportional number of non-local gates for entanglement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study, two datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments use two datasets, the breast cancer dataset with 30 features and the Iris dataset with 4 features, with no principal component analysis.
quotes: We use two datasets: one is the breast cancer dataset containing 30 features, and the other is the Iris dataset with 4 features.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that the link between qubit count, data separability and the number of CNOT gates needed is an experimental finding that still needs theoretical analysis.
quotes: Our experiments, while still needs theoretical analysis, reveal that, for the same dataset, higher-dimensional qubits may require an increased number of CNOT gates to achieve improved prediction accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the limit of its own evidence, Section 6.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method summary, numerical experiments and discussion of the main text; the supplemental material was only skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A classical statistical-mechanics inference method that combines tensor-network contraction with message passing to compute marginals on graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that their algorithm is exact for systems that are globally tree-like and locally dense-connected when the dense local graphs have limited treewidth.
quotes: Our algorithm is exact for systems that are globally tree-like and locally dense-connected when the dense local graphs have limited treewidth.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argued in the method section; not stated as a numbered theorem in the main text I read.
assertions.reader_inference: Classical method; bears on quantum ML only through its tensor-network tools and a mention of quantum error-correction decoding.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on a spin glass model on a real-world power grid network, TNMP gives much smaller errors than belief propagation, a loopy message-passing method and Markov chain Monte Carlo with many update steps.
quotes: In the figure, we can see that TNMP gives much smaller errors than belief propagation, the method in [16], and MCMC with a large number of updating steps.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one graph and one model family.

assertions.value: The authors state that computing local observables has the same complexity as computing the partition function, which falls in the class #P, so no polynomial algorithm solves it exactly in general.
quotes: The problem has the same complexity as computing the partition function and falls into the class of #P problems in mathematics, so there is no polynomial algorithm that solves the problem exactly in general.
assertions.certainty_reason: Background statement taken from prior work, not proved here.

papers.title_in_file: Power Characterization of Noisy Quantum Kernels
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, III main theorem statement and discussion, numerical section, V Conclusion; the appendix proofs were not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper showing that, under global depolarizing noise, quantum-kernel predictions concentrate on a fixed uninformative value as noisy layers increase, with a fashion-MNIST check.

assertions.value: The paper proves, under global depolarization noise, that the predictions of the optimal hypothesis of a noisy quantum kernel concentrate toward a fixed value, so noise can leave poor prediction capability even when the generalization error is small.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p1; Theorem III.1, Section III
quotes: Our results show that noises may make quantum kernel methods to only have poor prediction capability, even when the generalization error is small.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem III.1, Section III (proof in the appendix, not read by me).
assertions.reader_inference: The bound is for global depolarizing noise, which the authors say is weaker than the local noise models in related work.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results make a clear warning against using quantum kernel methods to demonstrate quantum advantage in the NISQ era, and that the results hold for a wide class of encoding strategies.
quotes: Our results hold for a wide class of quantum encoding strategies, and are applicable not only on shallow NISQ circuits, but also on future largescale quantum devices.
make a clear warning against utilizing quantum kernel methods to demonstrate quantum advantages in the NISQ era
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' interpretation of their theorem.
assertions.reader_inference: The warning rests on the global depolarizing noise model only.

assertions.value: The authors report a fashion-MNIST shirt versus dress experiment with 500 training samples, 500 test samples and 10 qubits, in which the training error shows a phase transition at L = 24 noisy layers and test predictions become no better than random guessing.
assertions.anchor: Section IV numerical experiments, Fig. 3, p7
quotes: There is a phase transition for the training error at L = 24.
In the numerical experiments, we utilize both training and test samples of size n = 500
the prediction is no better than the random guess
embed the 10-dimensional vector into the Hilbert space of N = 10 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated run on one dataset with a fixed noise rate.

papers.title_in_file: GroverGPT: A Large Language Model with 8 Billion Parameters for Quantum Searching
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, II results (accuracy and generalization), IV Conclusion and Outlook start; appendices and methods skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A fine-tuned 8-billion-parameter language model that predicts the outputs of Grover search circuits, used to probe classical simulability.

assertions.value: The authors report that, over 97K quantum search instances, GroverGPT outperformed GPT-4o (45% accuracy) and reached nearly 100% accuracy on 6- and 10-qubit datasets when trained on 4-qubit or larger datasets.
quotes: Analyzing 97K quantum search instances, GroverGPT consistently outperformed OpenAI's GPT-4o (45% accuracy), achieving nearly 100% accuracy on 6- and 10-qubit datasets when trained on 4-qubit or larger datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a single algorithm (Grover search).

assertions.value: The authors report that GroverGPT, trained on 3- to 6-qubit data, surpassed 95% accuracy on systems with over 20 qubits.
quotes: It also demonstrated strong generalization, surpassing 95% accuracy for systems with over 20 qubits when trained on 3- to 6-qubit data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The body text says accuracy declines to approximately 95% for 9 to 20 qubits and tests up to 20 qubits, so the abstract's 'over 20 qubits' is looser than the body.

assertions.value: The authors state that the model's capability decreases drastically as qubit count grows and is still limited by the exponential growth of the Hilbert space.
quotes: but the capability drastically decreases with the number of qubits (Section II C). This result indicates that the model somehow knows the structure of the algorithms, but the capability is still limited by the exponential growth of the Hilbert space.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limit, Section I and II C.

papers.title_in_file: QGHNN: A quantum graph Hamiltonian neural network
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, parts of V Experiments (Tables III to V discussion), VI Conclusion; sections III and IV derivations skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A parameterized quantum circuit method that maps a graph to a Hamiltonian and learns it, tested in PennyLane simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in PennyLane experiments, QGHNN outperforms the compared quantum models on all assessment metrics, with a lowest mean squared error of 0.004 and a maximum cosine similarity of 99.8%.
quotes: Experiments on the PennyLane quantum platform reveal that QGHNN outperforms all assessment metrics, achieving the lowest mean squared error of 0.004 and the maximum cosine similarity of 99.8%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small simulated graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the 99.8% accuracy and 0.004 mean squared error were reached when learning graph data with four qubits.
quotes: that the experimental accuracy of QGHNN can approach 99.8% when employing four qubits to learn graph data, with a mean squared error of 0.004.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scale of its best result, Section V.
assertions.reader_inference: Four qubits is a graph small enough to simulate exactly; the result says nothing about larger graphs.

assertions.value: The authors claim that QGHNN can reduce the impact of quantum noise and has potential for quantum knowledge graphs and recommendation systems.
quotes: QGHNN can reduce the impact of quantum noise and has significant potential application in future research of quantum knowledge graphs and recommendation systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim; I did not find a hardware noise experiment supporting it in the sections read.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum and Hybrid Machine-Learning Models for Materials-Science Tasks
papers.what_it_is: A small study applying quantum SVM and quantum neural network models, via Qiskit, to predict magnesium stacking fault energies from three elemental features.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best quantum SVM classification performance of 0.92 was reached with C = 1, reps = 3 and full entanglement, falling to 0.91 with linear entanglement.
quotes: The optimal performance of 0.92 is achieved for C = 1, reps=3, and full entanglement, which reduces marginally to 0.91 when we use the linear entanglement, keeping all other parameters identical.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: No classical baseline is reported in the sections read, so the result does not show any advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report hybrid quantum neural network classification accuracy of 0.810 at depth l = 1, 0.905 at l = 2 and 0.857 at l = 3.
quotes: The accuracy is 0.810 for l = 1, 0.905 for l = 2, and 0.857 for l = 3.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: The conclusion reports an optimum of 0.91 at depth l = 1 for this model, which conflicts with Section 3.3 (best at l = 2).

assertions.value: The authors state that the data are three elemental properties and stacking fault energies for elements in magnesium at a concentration of 6.25 at.%, so at most three qubits are needed.
quotes: The dataset used in this study is three elemental properties and the stacking fault energies (SFEs) when these elements appear in magnesium with a concentration of 6.25 at.% [25].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its dataset, Section 2.2.

assertions.value: The authors report finding hyperparameter combinations that yield validation scores of approximately 90% for the quantum SVM and the hybrid quantum neural network in both tasks.
quotes: We identify a few combinations of hyperparameters that yield validation scores of approximately 90% for QSVM and hybrid QNN in both tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Algorithms for Simulation of Lindblad Dynamics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, numerical results (scaling with system size), V Summary; the method derivations and appendices were skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A variational hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that simulates the Lindblad master equation and its adjoint for open quantum systems, benchmarked numerically.

assertions.value: The authors state that they design low-depth variational circuits that capture the unitary and non-unitary dynamics, and benchmark them on different system sizes.
quotes: We design and optimize low-depth variational quantum circuits that efficiently capture the unitary and non-unitary dynamics of the solutions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical benchmark on small simulated systems.

assertions.value: The authors report that the evaluation of the auto-correlation function does not deteriorate as system size increases in their simulations.
quotes: Notably, we observe that the evaluation of the auto-correlation function, as shown in the inset, does not deteriorate when increasing system size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result at small sizes, classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors expect that at large times the number of layers needed to keep fidelity below a threshold scales exponentially with system size, citing earlier work.
quotes: We expect, though, that at large times, the number of layers needed to maintain a fidelity below some threshold scales exponentially with system size, as shown in [32].
assertions.certainty_reason: An expectation attributed to other work, not shown here.
